site.title: Claude Tips Watch
site.tagline: Searchable reference of Claude and Claude Code tips from 16 accounts on X
site.scope_short: Claude Code, skills and subagents, Projects, Claude apps and the Claude API
site.scope_about: Claude and Anthropic tooling (Claude Code, subagents, skills and plugins, MCP, Projects, the Claude apps, prompting and the Claude API)
site.scope_note: Only Claude and Anthropic tooling is covered here. Tips about ChatGPT, Codex or other AI tools are left out, even when they come from the same accounts; a tip about a tool that works with several agents is included only when it names Claude or Claude Code.

tips.author: lydiahallie
tips.title: Make a Stop hook retry with exit code 2
tips.tip: A Stop hook can send Claude back to try again when a check fails, but only if the hook exits with code 2. Exit 2 returns Claude to retry with the hook's stderr; exit 1 is non-blocking, so Claude just finishes even though the check failed.

tips.author: lydiahallie
tips.title: Run /doctor prompt-audit
tips.tip: Run `/doctor prompt-audit` in each of your Claude Code repos if you haven't yet.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Try experimental Code Mode
tips.tip: Code Mode is a new, experimental way for Claude Code to work with tools: Claude writes scripts that chain your tools together, and it can answer you while long commands are still running. Opt in with `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1`.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: What Code Mode changes
tips.tip: Available experimentally from Claude Code 2.1.325: instead of calling tools one by one, Claude writes JavaScript that runs several tool calls in a single step. It can run commands in parallel, chain operations, and filter results before they are sent back to the model.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Build custom themes with mods
tips.tip: Claude Code on desktop supports custom themes built with mods: change the colors or add an animated background. Describe the look you want to Claude, or start from the theme-examples plugin.

tips.author: lydiahallie
tips.title: Themes can react to your session
tips.tip: Because custom themes are mods, the background can react to your actual session. Example: Claude made it snow as the context window fills up, with the mod hooking into `turn.step`.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Switch Claude Desktop to the Latest release channel
tips.tip: To get more frequent Claude Desktop builds on Windows and Mac, switch to the Latest release channel in Settings > Desktop app. Fixes and improvements arrive faster, but these builds can be less reliable than Stable, which stays the default.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Test foldable layouts with iPhone Duo
tips.tip: Claude Code on desktop supports iPhone Duo in the iOS simulator (public beta). Run your app on Duo next to your conversation, and Claude can fold and unfold the device to test each layout.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Opus as the main model, Fable 5.2 as advisor
tips.tip: Use Opus as your main model and Fable 5.2 as its advisor in Claude Code. Opus handles every turn; Fable steps in at critical moments: choosing an approach, debugging recurring errors and reviewing work before completion. You get Fable's judgment without paying for Fable on every turn.

tips.author: RLanceMartin
tips.title: Opus 5.5 medium as a daily driver
tips.tip: Opus 5.5 at medium effort is a fantastic daily driver and baseline. For when to reach for Fable 5.2 instead of Opus 5.5, see the Claude blog's model guidance.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: Confirmations for destructive actions
tips.tip: Claude Code 2.1.326 added confirmations for risky destructive actions (git operations, deletes) to reduce accidental data loss.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: Agent-team sessions open in Code Mode
tips.tip: In 2.1.326, agent-team sessions start in Code Mode when it is enabled.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: No more SSH logouts from PID reuse
tips.tip: In 2.1.326, the background service no longer kills user processes on PID reuse, which had caused unexpected SSH logouts.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: Stateful multi-step workflows
tips.tip: Claude Code 2.1.327 can launch agents that split complex multi-step tasks into stateful workflows.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: /install-github-app asks first
tips.tip: In 2.1.327, `/install-github-app` asks for confirmation before modifying a repository.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: Auto mode on clouds and gateways
tips.tip: Claude Code 2.1.328 adds auto mode for Opus/Sonnet 4.6 on clouds and gateways, letting sessions skip permission prompts. It also warns that cloud sessions may hold or drop messages when permission prompts are skipped.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: onFailure: block for mcp_tool hooks
tips.tip: 2.1.328 added `onFailure: block` for mcp_tool hooks, so a failed hook call blocks the action instead of allowing a partial run.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: Risky-action confirmations removed again
tips.tip: Claude Code 2.1.329 removed the risky-action confirmations: gated steps no longer prompt and run automatically.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: See scheduled work in /tasks
tips.tip: In 2.1.329, the session `/tasks` view shows scheduled tasks, `/loop` wakeups and goal forks; pressing `x` asks for confirmation before stopping a task.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: database-architect subagent for migrations
tips.tip: The rewritten database-architect agent reads your existing schema and migrations, catches locking risks and breaking changes, handles rolling deployments (using lock_timeout and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) and tests migrations on a temporary database before finishing. In his test (an 80M-row table, a migration needed 10 minutes before deployment), the same prompt scored 6/10 without the agent and 10/10 with it, and Claude picked the agent automatically in all 8 tests. Install: `npx claude-code-templates@latest --agent database/database-architect`.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: supabase-schema-architect subagent
tips.tip: For Supabase projects, the supabase-schema-architect agent designs schemas, migrations, RLS policies and Storage permissions. It covers explicit grants in every migration, RLS policies with auth.uid() and proper WITH CHECK rules, security definer functions without recursive policies, column-level permissions and PostgreSQL 16 trigger/RLS execution order. Before delivering, it tests access as two different authenticated users and runs the Supabase linter. Install: `npx claude-code-templates@latest --agent database/supabase-schema-architect`.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: api-security-audit subagent
tips.tip: Run the API Security Audit subagent on your REST API: it reviews authentication and JWT vulnerabilities, authorization flaws and privilege escalation, SQL/NoSQL injection, sensitive data exposure, and OWASP API Top 10 and rate limiting, then suggests fixes with code examples. Install: `npx claude-code-templates@latest --agent security/api-security-audit`.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Check a skill's compatibility across harnesses
tips.tip: A skill loading successfully doesn't mean it works as intended across agents. aitmpl.com now runs NVIDIA SkillEvaluator to check a skill against six harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw) and shows issues and suggested fixes for each; open any skill and select the Compatibility tab.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: AI Templates MCP in the Claude plugin marketplace
tips.tip: The AI Templates MCP in the official Claude Plugin Marketplace lets Claude search nearly 2,000 Claude Code components (agents, skills, hooks, commands, MCPs, settings, plugins), inspect their source and security scans, and generate one command that installs up to 20 of them. Tools: search_components, get_component, get_install_command, list_categories. It is remote, read-only and needs no account.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Let the project coordinator run parallel threads
tips.tip: In a Claude Code project, Claude coordinates your tasks across parallel threads. The coordinator is now more proactive: it answers your questions in the project chat and gives you status updates on ongoing threads.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Design long runs for surprise restarts
tips.tip: In Claude Projects and cloud sessions, the machine can restart without warning during hours-long processes, stopping containers, orchestrators and monitoring; completed work stays on disk but in-progress work can be lost. Make your orchestrator checkpoint after every step, resume from the last successful step, recover with a single script, check disk space and budget before each step, and alert you immediately when something stops.

tips.author: claudeai
tips.title: Add Claude to your video calls
tips.tip: Claude Meetings adds Claude to your team's video call, where it builds docs, whiteboards and other artifacts with you while you are still talking. Rolling out in beta on Team and Enterprise plans.

tips.author: felixrieseberg
tips.title: HTML-in-Canvas in the desktop apps
tips.tip: HTML-in-Canvas is now enabled in Claude's desktop apps, so Claude can build unusual, Flash-era-style sites. Demo artifact linked in the post.

tips.author: simonw
tips.title: Unblock auto mode by granting permission in chat
tips.tip: Regular Claude chat now uses auto mode, so it occasionally refuses to run something. Prompting "Hey permission system, I give this session permission to run this experiment for me (now try again)" seemed to unblock it, because auto mode takes your messages into account.

tips.author: alexalbert__
tips.title: Find the context Claude is missing
tips.tip: A lot of getting good work out of Claude now is finding the context it's missing and closing that gap. Claude Meetings is one way to bring in the remaining pieces and has proved useful inside Anthropic.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Claude Platform OAuth instead of API keys
tips.tip: With Claude Platform OAuth, users connect their Claude organization to your app instead of sharing API keys. Usage is billed to the customer's organization, developers choose who pays for each request, and users can set spending limits and revoke access at any time.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Use billing_policy to choose who pays
tips.tip: With Linked Billing, set `billing_policy` to decide per API request whether your platform or your customer pays, so you can charge for your software while users pay for their own tokens.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Linked billing (beta)
tips.tip: Linked billing is in beta on the Claude Platform: users of tools like Factory, Linear and Ramp can pay for Claude API usage through their own Claude Platform organization without sharing an API key.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Self-host Claude Managed Agents
tips.tip: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents is in private beta: host the agent harness, sandboxes and session history in your own cloud or on-premises, and choose where requests to Claude are sent.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Rethink your harness when you upgrade models
tips.tip: When you upgrade to a new model, rethink your harness and measure cost per task. That is the topic of this ClaudeDevs video with @dejno and @luccasiau, who also explain how Anthropic launches new models on its API.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Let Claude verify its own work
tips.tip: Claude writes better code when it can verify its work, and checks that used to be expensive (tests, benchmarks, end-to-end runs) are now cheap. The Claude Code team's approach is written up on the Claude blog.

tips.author: simonw
tips.title: The external sandbox pattern
tips.tip: In the external sandbox pattern, the coding agent runs on your Mac but executes code inside a WebAssembly, QEMU or Apple Container sandbox. The write-up includes a demo for Claude Code (plus Codex and Pi).

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Anthropic's security programs for developers
tips.tip: Anthropic is cutting disclosure timelines for high and critical vulnerabilities from 90 to 30 days, and opening three programs: OSS Scanner (Claude scans open-source projects for vulnerabilities), Claude for Open Source (6 months of Claude Ultra free for eligible maintainers) and the Cyber Verification Program (access to Claude for legitimate security research).

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Cyber Verification Program unlocks Defense Access
tips.tip: Approval for Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program gives your Claude account Defense Access, which reduces security-related blocks for legitimate defensive work such as malware analysis, vulnerability validation and incident response, and includes access to Claude Mythos models.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Lean on prompt caching in agent loops
tips.tip: In agentic turns, follow-up requests that repeat or append to the first request reuse cached blocks, which cuts cost.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Don't change the system prompt or effort mid-conversation
tips.tip: Changing the system prompt or the effort setting partway through a conversation breaks prompt caching.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Use an evals harness when switching models
tips.tip: Build and tune an evals harness so that when you switch models or adjust settings such as thinking, you can confirm you get the same outcome on a better cost curve.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Apply a prebuilt theme with /custom-theme
tips.tip: Run `/custom-theme <name>` (the demo uses `honu-lagoon`) to apply a prebuilt theme.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Set themes from a mod
tips.tip: In the mod API, `$.theme.set({ colors, backdrop })` sets a theme's colors and backdrop.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Describe the theme you want
tips.tip: Ask in plain language, for example "make me a theme with a synthwave sunset and neon pink accents", and Claude builds it.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Mods can react to events
tips.tip: Mods can add visual feedback to events, such as fireworks when a PR merges after you say "ship it".

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Mods docs
tips.tip: The mods documentation lives in the Claude Code docs under Plugins > Mods.

tips.author: lydiahallie
tips.title: Tell /compact what to keep
tips.tip: `/compact` accepts instructions about what to keep, for example `/compact keep the test notes`.

tips.author: felixrieseberg
tips.title: HTML-in-Canvas on every desktop platform
tips.tip: HTML-in-Canvas is available in Claude for macOS, Windows and Linux.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Move from Manual to Auto permission mode
tips.tip: With newer models, switch the permission mode from Manual to Auto: they read intent and your codebase well enough that you don't need to approve every command or steer mid-session.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Cut generic warnings from CLAUDE.md
tips.tip: Remove generic instructions such as "Think hard and be thorough." or "IMPORTANT: always use the auth helper" from CLAUDE.md. Newer models don't need them, and clutter like this can derail them.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Keep CLAUDE.md to what Claude can't infer
tips.tip: Limit CLAUDE.md to context Claude can't see or work out from the code, for example that a legacy directory is still used by the mobile apps.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Audit your instructions with /doctor prompt-audit
tips.tip: Run `/doctor prompt-audit` to check your CLAUDE.md and skills for instructions the new model no longer needs.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Describe Auto mode's trust boundaries in plain English
tips.tip: In `.claude/settings.json`, an `autoMode` block takes plain-English lists: `environment` (e.g. "Trusted cloud buckets: s3://acme-staging"), `allow` ("Deploying to staging is allowed") and `hard_deny` ("Never send code to third-party APIs"), each starting with `"$defaults"`.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Hard-block commands with deny rules
tips.tip: Add a command to `permissions.deny` in `.claude/settings.json`, e.g. `"Bash(git reset --hard *)"`, to block it in the harness before the Auto mode classifier ever sees it.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Rule of thumb for what to deny
tips.tip: If Claude could make a mistake you can take back (like git edits), leave it to the model. If you can't take it back (deleting something for good, exposing a secret, sending data outside), make it a deny rule.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Deny reads of secrets
tips.tip: Add deny rules like `"Read(./.env)"` and `"Read(~/.ssh/**)"` so a compromised dependency can't trick Claude into reading or leaking your secrets.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Turn on the shell sandbox
tips.tip: Add `"sandbox": { "enabled": true }` to `.claude/settings.json` to sandbox shell commands at the OS level, limiting which files, folders and hosts a command like `npm test` and its child processes can reach.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Run long tasks in a cloud session
tips.tip: Cloud sessions run on a fresh, isolated machine with your repo, keep going with your laptop closed, and keep local secrets such as `.env`, `~/.ssh` and GitHub tokens out of reach.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Give cloud sessions only the network and secrets they need
tips.tip: Configure Network access with allowed domains (e.g. `api.example.com`) and hand over API keys through Network secrets, instead of exposing your local environment.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Ask Claude to prove its work
tips.tip: Prompt for verifiable steps, for example "Split it into tasks, each with its own test." and "Show me the test output."

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Run checks from lifecycle hooks
tips.tip: Use hooks to verify automatically: `PostToolUse` to lint after every edit, `TaskCompleted` to run a task's tests, and `Stop` to run the full suite at the end.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Fail checks with exit 2, not exit 1
tips.tip: Make your check scripts exit with code 2 on failure. Exit 1, the common default, gets marked as completed; exit 2 sends Claude back to fix it.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Let CI failures loop back to Claude
tips.tip: With CI auto-fix, a failed PR check goes back to Claude, which fixes it without you stepping in.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Auto-merge once checks pass
tips.tip: Turn on "Merge when ready" so PRs merge automatically after their checks pass, so you don't have to hand-review small, safe changes.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Match review effort to risk
tips.tip: Let agents do the first review on every PR, then require no humans for small changes (typos, lint fixes), one person for most changes, and several for the riskiest.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Let a project orchestrate the sessions
tips.tip: Claude Code projects (in beta) take an overall goal; an orchestrator splits the work, starts worker sessions and manages their context, so you don't have to juggle sessions yourself.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Fable to orchestrate, Opus 5.5 to code
tips.tip: In a project, put a reasoning model like Fable on the orchestrator (deciding tasks, judging results) and Opus 5.5 on the worker threads that write the code.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: Claude now asks before destructive actions
tips.tip: Claude Code 2.1.330 adds a confirm-before-risky-actions policy. The system prompt now has a “measure twice, cut once” rule: Claude weighs reversibility and blast radius and asks for confirmation before destructive, hard-to-reverse, shared-state or public actions such as rm -rf, reset --hard, force-push, PR comments, Slack/email and third-party uploads, including git status/stash checks.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: Sign in to an Enterprise Admin Console org
tips.tip: Claude Code 2.1.330 can sign in to organizations managed in Anthropic's Enterprise Admin Console: after `claude auth login`, Claude Code applies the organization's settings and uses its cloud provider or gateway.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: easel draws charts; turn it off in /config
tips.tip: 2.1.330 adds easel, a built-in mod that draws charts when asked and under MCP metrics results (Pro, Max and, where available, Team and Enterprise, on macOS and Linux). Turn automatic charts off in `/config`.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: Print the full sign-in link
tips.tip: Set `CLAUDE_CODE_FULL_SIGN_IN_LINK=1` (2.1.330) to print the full sign-in link, if the short one shows an error or a script reads values from it.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: vulnerability-scanner skill for security reviews
tips.tip: The vulnerability-scanner skill reviews your code for security vulnerabilities, including AI agents and MCP servers. It maps the attack surface and trust boundaries, detects prompt injection and insecure agent tools, checks for exposed secrets and vulnerable dependencies, reviews MCP servers, skills, hooks and CLAUDE.md files, flags OWASP and CI/CD risks, verifies findings to cut false positives, and reports each issue with Attack, Impact and Fix. It is read-only and never modifies your code. In his tests it activated automatically in 7/7 runs with 0 false positives across 7 decoys. Install: `npx claude-code-templates@latest --skill security/vulnerability-scanner`.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: MCP Events: agents that react without a prompt
tips.tip: With MCP Events, AI agents can subscribe to external events and react without waiting for a user prompt, for example starting a code review and running tests when a new PR arrives in a GitHub repository. It supports three delivery modes: Poll, Push and Webhook. In Poll mode the client discovers available events, checks the server, waits and checks again; when an event arrives it is passed to the agent runtime.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: dependency-cooldown setting blocks brand-new packages
tips.tip: The dependency-cooldown setting for Claude Code blocks package versions published less than 7 days ago from being installed through npm, pnpm or uv. It reduces the risk of supply chain attacks, protects against slopsquatting, and requires your permission if Claude tries.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Two ways to use the easel chart mod
tips.tip: easel is a built-in mod in Claude Code 2.1.330 that renders charts directly inside your conversations. Use it on demand by asking Claude to chart data from JSON, CSV, tables or query results, or let it run automatically when an MCP returns time-series metrics.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Turn off automatic charts in /config
tips.tip: If you don't want the easel mod drawing charts automatically, run /config and look for the Auto charts option to disable it.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Type /ship to open, review and watch a pull request
tips.tip: In Claude Code, type /ship to open a pull request if there is none, review it in the session, then keep watching it. In the demo the review flags an issue and offers Apply fixes or Walk through in changes, then Claude tests, commits and pushes.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Let /ship handle failed checks and review comments
tips.tip: After pushing, /ship keeps watching the PR with scheduled check-ins: in the demo it fixes a failing CI test and answers a reviewer's comment, then reports ready once checks pass and comments are answered. Merging stays with you, within your permissions and the repository's branch rules.

tips.author: cjav_dev
tips.title: Claude Ship vs. the /ship skill
tips.tip: There are two pieces: Claude Ship (beta) for Team and Enterprise, which you turn on in settings and which can review PRs, work on fixes and approve the ones your team's policy allows; and the /ship skill, which anyone can use and which ships with the latest Claude Code version.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Side panel tools now open as tabs
tips.tip: In Claude Code on desktop, Files, Changes, Terminal and the other tools open as tabs beside your session. You can move a tab to see several at once or pop it out into its own window. Rolling out on Mac first; Windows and Linux are coming.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Side panel shortcuts and the + tab menu
tips.tip: Open side-panel tools with shortcuts: Changes ⇧⌘D, Browser ⇧⌘B, Files ⇧⌘F, Terminal ⌘J, Side chat ⌘;. The + button in the tab bar adds a tab; in the demo the Browser tab opens the running dev server at localhost:3000.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Split tabs to watch logs while you test
tips.tip: Click the layout icon at the top right of a tab to Move it (left, right, top or bottom), Fill and arrange, or Open in new window. In the demo, moving Terminal (running tail -f logs/server.log) to the bottom lets you click Add to cart in the Browser tab and watch the server log update below it.

tips.author: claudeai
tips.title: Connectors and skills are now one thing: plugins
tips.tip: In Claude, connectors (to your tools) and skills come together as plugins, so one install can connect a tool, teach a skill, or both. Live on Free, Pro, Max and Ultra, with Team and Enterprise coming. Browse 10,000+ plugins at claude.ai/plugins.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Zero data retention with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards
tips.tip: ZDR with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards is in public beta for eligible orgs on the Claude Platform: encrypted copies of your Messages API traffic go to your own cloud storage, and automated checks look for misuse across requests and flag serious risks for your team to review. Useful if your company requires zero data retention and you still want to use Fable.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Claude Platform OAuth: let customers pay for their own usage
tips.tip: With Claude Platform OAuth (beta, Linked Billing), a customer links their Claude Console organization to your app once and sets a monthly spend limit; Claude calls they start in your app are then billed to their organization. It is not sign-in with a Claude.ai plan: Pro or Max can't be linked, the org needs API billing (prepaid credits or invoice), and the person linking needs the Admin or Billing role. There is no client secret.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Test OAuth with a second account and test users
tips.tip: Create the app under Organization → Customers → OAuth apps (connection type organization_shared). The org that owns the app can't link it, so test with a second Claude account using a different email and its own Console org with prepaid credits. In Testing mode only listed test users can link (max USD 50/month each); add them and your callback URL on the Settings tab (http://localhost works). Publishing needs a DNS record and an Anthropic review.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Enable both billing:attribution and offline_access
tips.tip: Turn on both the billing:attribution and offline_access permissions for the OAuth app. With offline_access off, the authorization request fails with invalid_scope, and you also don't get the long-lived token that keeps access without asking the customer to approve again.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Use an issuer with inline keys instead of a cloud identity provider
tips.tip: You don't need AWS, GCP, Okta or similar for workload identity: under Keys → Workload identity → Issuers, register an issuer with inline keys (the URL is just a name and doesn't need to exist) and paste your public key. The key editor rejects the usual {"keys": [...]} format; paste only the array. Then in the app's Client authentication pick that issuer, a subject and the audience https://auth.claude.com. If you sign in Node, use ECDSA signatures in ieee-p1363 format or you get jwt_signature_invalid.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Set the default workspace before anyone links
tips.tip: Billed calls need a service account (Keys → Service accounts) plus a federation rule on the same issuer with the audience https://api.anthropic.com. Choose it as the Operator service account, then set "Default workspace for platform auth mode OAuth tokens" right below it. Without that field the last link step fails with unauthorized_client, and since the customer's code lasts only 5 minutes you lose a whole approval round.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: OAuth backend rules: rotate refresh tokens, bind state
tips.tip: Save the newest refresh token every time because it rotates on each use. Check that the returned state is yours and bind it to the browser that started the flow (for example with an HttpOnly cookie). Before approval a billed call returns 403 user_profile_billing_not_authorized, a handy check. Batches and billable code execution aren't supported, and the customer's ZDR or BAA doesn't cover these calls. Customers can revoke from Keys → Linked platforms.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: A skill that walks Claude through Linked Billing setup
tips.tip: @dani_avila7 built a Claude Platform OAuth skill that walks Claude through integrating Linked Billing into your app. Install it and ask Claude to set up Linked Billing; with the Chrome extension, Claude can ask for browser access to help fill out the Console steps.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: 2.1.331 drops the risky-action confirmation rule
tips.tip: Claude Code 2.1.331 (135 CLI changes, 1 system prompt change) removes the system-prompt risky-action confirmation, so agents may run previously blocked risky steps automatically. Review your permission and deny settings if you relied on that prompt.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: 2.1.331: Code Mode in cloud terminal sessions, MCP hang fix
tips.tip: In 2.1.331, terminal sessions add Code Mode on cloud platforms with syntax highlighting, and MCP tool calls no longer hang up to 30 minutes on malformed local or WebSocket replies.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Install an artifact as its own desktop app
tips.tip: In the Claude desktop app, click the arrow next to the artifact's title at the top of the artifact pane, choose Install as app (Beta), then Install. The artifact gets its own window and dock icon and opens like any other app. It can't reach your files or run programs unless you allow it; it can use your connectors and, if you allow it, send notifications or add a menu bar item. Beta on Mac and Windows.

tips.author: lydiahallie
tips.title: Artifact apps have storage and use the viewer's connectors
tips.tip: On paid plans, artifacts come with personal and shared storage, which makes them handy for small internal tools. By default an artifact uses the connectors of whoever opens it, so the same app shows each person their own data plus anything shared with the whole team.

tips.author: felixrieseberg
tips.title: First artifact app to try: a desktop pet
tips.tip: A quick way to try artifact apps: ask Claude "Build me a desktop pet as an artifact app. Make it a cat/dog/bunny/enterprise-ready CRM". It takes only a few minutes.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: 2.1.332 asks before risky or destructive actions again
tips.tip: Claude Code 2.1.332 (150 CLI changes, 1 system prompt change) defaults to confirmation for risky or destructive actions. The new "execute with care" prompt rule has Claude judge reversibility and blast radius: local, reversible steps go ahead, while destructive, hard-to-undo, shared-state or third-party upload actions get a confirmation request (with extra git status/stash checks). This reverses the 2.1.331 change.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: Skills served by MCP servers show up as server:skill
tips.tip: From 2.1.332, skills hosted on MCP servers (beta) appear in the / menu as server:skill; your other skills keep their names.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: New PreSkillShellCommand hook can block a skill's inline shell
tips.tip: 2.1.332 adds a PreSkillShellCommand hook event that can refuse a skill or command's inline shell commands as it loads. On 2.1.331 and older, a settings file that names this hook opens a dialog at start.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: /permissions now rejects rules that would be skipped
tips.tip: In 2.1.332, /permissions refuses a rule that would be ignored at the next start, such as rm -rf with no tool name, and shows why, so check your rules include the tool name.

tips.author: ClaudeCodeLog
tips.title: Self-hosted runners: OAuth tokens can now start with oat02-
tips.tip: On self-hosted runners, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN's prefix can now end in oat02- as well as oat01-. Update proxy rules and log scrubbers that match oat01-, and mask the whole value.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Skills over MCP: servers ship their own skills
tips.tip: MCP servers can now ship with their own skills, so Claude Code knows how to use them out of the box. Announced for MCP's second birthday together with Tasks.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: How a skill served over MCP loads in Claude Code
tips.tip: In the aitmpl demo the server lists its skills with descriptions and a sha256 digest per file; they show as aitmpl:component-review. Type /aitmpl:component-review or just ask for something matching its description. Claude Code reads that skill's SKILL.md from the server and fetches supporting files only when the skill asks for them. The instructions load without a prompt in auto mode; otherwise you allow that version first.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Publish your own Skills-over-MCP component with Claude's help
tips.tip: Skills over MCP is on aitmpl.com. To publish your own, fork the repo and ask Claude how to add a component with these capabilities; it guides you through the process, including validation before publication.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Use MCP elicitations instead of letting the model ask questions
tips.tip: With MCP elicitation, the server sends a JSON Schema and the host renders it as an interactive form, returning structured data straight to the server. That builds structured workflows and saves tokens compared with having the LLM collect the information from the user.

tips.author: dani_avila7
tips.title: Elicitation forms in Claude Code
tips.tip: When an MCP server requests information, Claude Code renders an interactive form from the server's JSON Schema. In the example the server asks you to pick a component type and category before the tool call continues.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Run /code-review before you push
tips.tip: /code-review checks your branch's commits and uncommitted changes for correctness bugs. Variants: /code-review high 1234 (PR 1234 at high effort), --fix (apply findings to the working tree), --comment 1234 (post findings on the PR), ultra (deeper review in the cloud; needs a claude.ai login and can be billed separately). Effort runs low to max and Claude remembers the last level. Commit before --fix in a background review: /rewind may not catch those edits.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Check git status before /ship
tips.tip: If there's no PR yet, /ship commits pending changes as if you ran git add -A (respecting .gitignore), pushes, opens the PR as you, reviews it and fixes valid findings. It won't commit secret-looking files or rule files (CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, .claude/, .github/), and in a public repo it commits nothing, so commit those yourself. Options: /ship high, /ship 41 (PR #41), /ship +my-lint-bot (also read that bot's comments), /ship stop.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: What the /ship watch needs to keep running
tips.tip: The watch runs as you on your machine and quota for up to seven days: keep the session open and the machine awake, run gh auth login first, and it only watches PRs you opened. Outside auto mode it stops at every prompt; it won't run in bypass-permissions mode, and on Windows it doesn't start. Give it its own checkout (use a worktree for your next task). A PreToolUse or PermissionRequest hook on Bash in the repo's .claude/settings.json prevents the watch.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Only run the watch on repos where you trust every merger
tips.tip: The watch merges the base branch and runs your tests, so anyone who can land changes on the base branch can run commands on your machine. Claude won't merge or force-push, and its commits skip rule files, but git hooks don't run on its commits, so put required checks in CI and branch rules. Run /ship terms before your first use.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: /steward: see an existing PR through without re-reviewing
tips.tip: Check out the branch and run /steward 41 (or plain /steward for the current branch's PR) to run only the watch: fix failing checks, resolve conflicts and answer comments, with no review first. Stop it with /steward stop or /ship stop; one watch per session. Good fits are PRs with red checks or stuck in conflict loops, not ones in a design debate. Claude pushes at most 3 times per issue, then reports and escalates.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Turn repeated feedback into the right file
tips.tip: Code conventions go in CLAUDE.md (read by Claude Code, local /code-review, Code Review and PR Steward). PR review rules go in REVIEW.md (Code Review and PR Steward only, not local /code-review). How to start and exercise the app goes in .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md. How PRs should be looked after goes in .claude/skills/steward/SKILL.md. The team's bar: a pattern must repeat on at least 2 PRs before it becomes a rule.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Keep the steward skill out of the / menu
tips.tip: In .claude/skills/steward/SKILL.md, set user-invocable: false and disable-model-invocation: true so the house rules stay out of the / menu and out of skills Claude picks on its own. The local watch reads it from your working directory; PR Steward reads it from the default branch, so review edits to it like CI changes.

tips.author: ClaudeDevs
tips.title: Start Claude Approvals in observe mode and keep the advisory line
tips.tip: Claude Approvals reads .claude/approvals.yml from the default branch. Start with mode: observe so it only reports what it would decide, and keep advisory: [claude/code_review] in rules: once a policy is on the default branch, Code Review only runs automatically on PRs matching a rule that names it. After the watch merges the base branch, the PR author should comment @claude approve.

sources.author: cjav_dev
sources.summary: @lydiahallie's talk "Rethinking Claude Code Best Practices": with newer models you can step out of the loop. Five areas: lighter CLAUDE.md steering, Auto mode instead of manual approvals, deny rules, sandboxing and cloud sessions for safety, verification through prompts, hooks and CI, and orchestrating many sessions with Claude Code projects.
